structured.answer: According to the page, I'd open the account at פסגות (marked "הזול") and buy "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125". With 10,000 ₪ now and 500 ₪ a month, it says I'd have about 86,045 ₪ after ten years. But that's on the page's example of 7% a year, and פסגות isn't a bank, so I won't do anything until I've asked my son.

stuck.why: It says 'your choice' but I never chose פסגות. The page chose it, and I didn't know why at first.
It says 'לדוגמה של האתר'. I don't know if 7% is a promise or a guess, and the 86,045 depends on it.
Every fund has a minus (−0.04%, −1,030 ₪). I almost backed away from all of them before I found the small explanation at the bottom of the list.
There's a price for women from 60, which is me, but it says 'סגור למצטרפים'. I'm not sure if that still helps an old customer.

findings.what: Every fund shows a minus in red-ish purple (−0.04%, −1,030 ₪). It scares you away, and the explanation of what the minus means is only at the bottom of the list, in small grey text
Dark background with grey text. The smaller lines (the 'לא בחישוב' notes, the explanations) are hard to read even enlarged
The return of 7% is the site's example, but the big 86,045 looks like a promise. There is no word about losing
It says 'הבחירה שלכם' about something the site picked for me
The first screen opens with English letters (MSCI, S&P). Someone like me would leave there
Sliders for the amounts. Good thing there are also boxes to type in
Too many numbers in the cost comparison (18 ₪ more, 1,390 ₪ less, 342 ₪ more). I couldn't tell which is good
Red and orange and yellow bars that are close in colour, and the key for them is far away
The senior price at הפועלים is 'סגור למצטרפים' with no explanation of who still gets it
